hero_short: AI now drafts the résumés and the cover letters, so sounding capable has never been cheaper. A senior professional has to show the work instead, and I chose to lead that shift rather than wait for it. This site is my most advanced front-end build to date and the most important piece of my personal brand, designed and built by me with AI in five months. Scroll on for why it had to exist, how it grew from a single page, how it was built, and the figures that prove it.
act0_verdict: AI is rewriting work faster than careers can adapt.
act0_lede: Three shifts that make a proven personal brand urgent in 2026.
act0_s1_t: A fifth of jobs in motion
act0_s1_x: By 2030, 22% of today's jobs will be disrupted, with 170 million created and 92 million displaced, and 39% of the skills workers rely on are expected to change.
act0_s2_x: Young workers in the most AI-exposed jobs lost 13% of their employment since 2022, though the cause may not be AI alone. Across Latin America, 26–38% of jobs are exposed to generative AI; in Lima, the under-25 share of work has fallen by about a third since 2019.
act0_s3_x: 66% of leaders would not hire someone without AI skills, and 71% would choose a less experienced candidate who has them. Differentiation for 2027 has to be shown, not claimed, in 2026.
act0_foot: Sources: World Economic Forum, Future of Jobs Report 2025; Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Atkinson and Yamco, 6 January 2026; ILO and World Bank, Working Paper 121, 2024; Microsoft and LinkedIn, Work Trend Index 2024; INEI, Encuesta Permanente de Empleo Nacional, May–July 2026.
act1_verdict: Credentials open the door. They don't prove what I can build.
act1_lede: Three reasons a strong résumé is no longer enough.
act1_s1_x: Job posts spell out what a candidate must have, never how they are expected to think or sound. Meeting every requirement gets an application read; being understood gets it believed.
act1_s2_x: Despite their value, not a single one of my flagship academic credentials (an MBA, a MicroMasters and a Microsoft specialization) evidences what I can actually build. Since a work sample predicts performance about 3× better than education, this live page translates those honors into an irrefutable legacy.
act1_s3_x: Three in four hiring teams say they receive AI-written applications, and 65% of hiring managers find skills harder to verify. When anyone can write a fluent claim in seconds, only a verifiable build stands out.
act1_foot: Sources: Sackett et al. (2022) on selection validity; Robert Half, November 2025, n = 2,000+; Deel Global Hiring Report 2026.
act2_verdict: Three levels of fidelity, one direction.
act2_lede: From renting a template to directing every line.
act2_s1_x: My first portfolios ran on Canva, Figma and Framer from 2023 to 2025. None matched the fidelity my design and my authority as a UX educator demanded, and learning to code meant a new degree and starting over as a junior.
act2_s2_x: It was never about prompting AI for a website to brag about. Weeks on this compact one-scroll page gave me the flight hours no university could, testing and locking the AI workflows that built the multi-page site you are reading.
act2_s3_x: The version you are reading: dedicated About and Contact pages, four copy-tested case briefs, my most capable front-end to date, and the Microsoft specialization finished.
act2_foot: Building a site with AI in 2027 takes more than a prompt: it takes a whole orchestration, from research to review. That is what sets this build apart from audacious vibe-coders and from developers who still write every line by hand.

act4_verdict: Six decisions, four of them multi-page.
act4_lede: What held from the start, and what the multi-page build added.
act4_c1_x: No framework, no build step, no dependency I cannot read end to end.
act4_c1_rv_txt: Nothing to migrate when a major version lands. No security-patch treadmill. A payload small enough to stay fast on a mid-range phone over Peruvian mobile data — which is what most recruiters will use to open it.
act4_c2_x: WCAG AA held as a build gate, usable with screen readers and keyboards.
act4_c2_rv_txt1: Every meaningful image carries alt text, every control is reachable by keyboard with a visible focus state, and contrast is verified in both themes rather than assumed.
act4_c2_rv_txt2: Layout resolves at three declared breakpoints — 767px and below, 768 to 1023, and 1024 up.
act4_c3_x: Site chrome, the strings every brief shares, and each brief's own copy, merged in that order.
act4_c3_rv_txt1: A key lives at one level only, so a label every brief shares changes once, for all of them.
act4_c3_rv_txt3: Every English file has a Spanish twin with the same keys, checked by script before each commit.
act4_c4_x: Acts, poster panels, charts and dashboards, shared by every case brief.
act4_c4_rv_txt1: Each case gets its own route and its own dictionary, so a recruiter can be sent to one page rather than to a scroll position. The cost: one defect in the chassis is a defect in every brief.
act4_c5_x: Every stage is written down as a dispatch before any code changes.
act4_c5_rv_txt: A written brief, then a prompt with preflight checks, then a plan I approve. The build stops at each gate on a local server until I release it with a set phrase, and it ends in a completion report. AI executes; the standard, the review and every merge stay with me.
act4_c6_x: This build runs under a locked scope against overthinking.
act4_c6_rv_txt: Improvements that fall outside the written scope are logged in one line and not built. Decisions are made once, recorded as numbered rulings and not reopened. The discipline is the deliverable as much as the site is.

act6_p1_x: A run stops at every gate until I release it. Review happens on the running page before changes are effective in live build.
